standard_prerequisites.name: At-worst-nodal schemes of relative dimension one, étale extensions of discrete valuation rings and the node equation
standard_prerequisites.statement: A scheme of relative dimension one over a discrete valuation ring is at-worst-nodal when its singularities are ordinary double points whose branches are smooth; in a neighbourhood of such a point the local equation can be put in the form of a product of two coordinate functions, possibly with a power of the uniformizer subtracted, after an étale extension of the ring and after an étale modification of the scheme. An étale extension of discrete valuation rings is an extension that is flat and unramified, and Dedekind domains admit étale extensions realising prescribed residue extensions only under a separability condition; a morphism to an affine space which is smooth at a point is étale after shrinking. The author's own lemmas of the chapter and the quoted results of the More on Algebra, Morphisms and Curves chapters are the allowed inputs.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted lemma is the local model on which the chapter's resolution of at-worst-nodal schemes by blowups is carried out, and the following lemmas of the section compute with this model.

core_obligations: Choose an étale neighbourhood making the residue extension separable: after passing to an étale extension of the discrete valuation ring, the point may be assumed to have a rational residue field, and the local ring of the scheme at the point is then a discrete valuation ring or an ordinary double point (source lines 6132-6150).

Split into the two forms of the local equation: in the regular case the local ring is a discrete valuation ring and the equation can be taken to be the product of the two variables; in the nodal case the equation is the product of the two variables minus a power of the uniformizer, and the exponent is determined by the local computation (source lines 6150-6175).

Assemble the diagram: the étale extensions of the ring and of the scheme fit into the commutative diagram displayed in the statement, and the morphism from the étale neighbourhood to the affine spectrum of the quotient ring is étale at the point, which is what the statement asserts (source lines 6175-6188).

proof_roadmap.step: Pass to an étale extension of the ring so that the residue extension becomes separable and the local analysis applies.
Derive the two possible forms of the local equation at the point.
Fit the étale neighbourhood and the affine model into the commutative diagram of the statement.
